After: the scores are rescaled linearly into the default range 0.5 to 1.0 and written as each node's size, so F becomes 0.5 and B 1.0, with every node drawn in proportion." width="100%"} Linearly maps numeric node values onto a target interval and writes the results to another node attribute, `size` by default, modifying the graph in place. The smallest input value maps to the lower end of `range=`, the largest to the upper end, and everything else proportionally in between (min-max scaling). The source attribute is not changed. This is mainly used to turn analysis results into visual encodings, for example: - sizing nodes by centrality, degree, or PageRank so important nodes stand out - putting measures with very different scales onto a common interval before comparing or combining them - producing an inverted scale (large values -> small output) by giving a reversed range Only the minimum and maximum of the values matter, so a single outlier can compress every other node toward one end of the range. If all values are equal, every node receives the lower bound of `range=`. Values must be numeric; non-numeric values raise a `TypeError`. The mapping is recorded on the graph and listed under "Node aesthetics" by `describe()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr_from]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the numeric node attribute to read (e.g., `"betweenness_centrality"`, `"score"`). Nodes without this attribute are left unchanged. Ignored for reading when `values=` is given (it is then only used to label the recorded aesthetic). Default is `None`; either this or `values=` must be supplied. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, int | float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dict mapping nodes to numeric values, keyed by node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). Use this to rescale data that isn't stored as an attribute, such as the output of a `return_dict=True` computation. If given, it takes precedence over `node_attr_from=` and `nodes=`. Default is `None`. [node_attr_to]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["size"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that receives the rescaled values. Default is `"size"`, which the interactive graph widget uses for node size. Existing values in this attribute are overwritten for the rescaled nodes. Writing back to the same name as `node_attr_from=` replaces the original values. [range]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A two-element list `[low, high]` giving the output interval. Default is `None`, which means `[0.5, 1.0]`. Sizes within `[0, 1]` are treated by the graph widget as relative values and scaled to pixels, while larger numbers are used as given. If `low` is greater than `high`, the scale is inverted. [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list[str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of node IDs or labels restricting which nodes are read from `node_attr_from=`. The minimum and maximum are then computed over these nodes only. If `None` (the default), all nodes are considered. Ignored when `values=` is given. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If neither `node_attr_from=` nor `values=` is provided, or if `range=` does not contain exactly two values. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~colorize_node_attrs`) : Map categorical values to colors. [](`~plot`) : Size a static plot by an attribute directly, with `size_by=`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} By default the values are mapped linearly onto 0.5 to 1.0 and written to `size`. The lowest score maps to 0.5, the highest to 1.0, and the one halfway between to 0.75: ::: {#61f47462 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes( {"A": {"score": 6}, "B": {"score": 2}, "C": {"score": 10}} ) graph.rescale_node_attrs("score") graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: A reversed `range=` inverts the scale, so the largest value gets the smallest result: ::: {#162dc956 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.rescale_node_attrs("score", node_attr_to="rank", range=[3, 1]) graph.get_node_df().select("label", "score", "size", "rank") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### One score from two measures Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33). Degree counts a member's ties, and betweenness measures how often a member lies on the shortest paths between others. Degrees run to 17 and betweenness only to 0.44, so adding them as they are would rank by degree alone. Rescaling both onto 0 to 1 lets them count equally: ::: {#946cd7b3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl karate = ec.karate_club() ties = karate.degrees(return_dict=True) between = karate.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) karate.rescale_node_attrs(values=ties, node_attr_to="ties", range=[0, 1]) karate.rescale_node_attrs( values=between, node_attr_to="between", range=[0, 1] ) score = (pl.col("ties") + pl.col("between")) / 2 nodes = karate.get_node_df().with_columns(score=score) nodes.sort("score", descending=True).head(6).select( "label", "degree", "ties", "between", "score" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

Sized by the combined score: ::: {#696612ad .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.set_node_attrs("score", dict(nodes.select("id", "score").rows())) karate.plot( size_by="score", color_by="faction", label_by="label", seed=4 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
